quote: GRPO foregoes the critic model, instead estimating the baseline from group scores, significantly reducing training resources compared to Proximal Policy Optimization (PPO).
reason: With one terminal reward the critic is unnecessary: "GRPO foregoes the critic model, instead estimating the baseline from group scores, significantly reducing training resources compared to Proximal Policy Optimization (PPO)." [@shao2024]; RLOO and ReMax also drop it [@ahmadian2024; @li2024].
note: Quote supports critic dropped in GRPO. Q(x,y)=r is not in this passage; RLOO and ReMax not quoted.

quote: usually only the last token is assigned a reward score by the reward model, which may complicate the training of a value function that is accurate at each token.
reason: Only the final token is rewarded: "usually only the last token is assigned a reward score by the reward model, which may complicate the training of a value function that is accurate at each token." [@shao2024]
note: Passage is about a reward model, not a verifiable rule reward; supports a degenerate per-token value only by analogy.

quote: score the generated steps according to the PRM’s predicted step-wise reward-to-go estimate (which also corresponds to the total reward from the prefix since the reward is sparse in this setting)
reason: The PRM acts as a value over prefixes: "score the generated steps according to the PRM’s predicted step-wise reward-to-go estimate (which also corresponds to the total reward from the prefix since the reward is sparse in this setting)" [@snell2024]; it drives search of the AlphaZero shape [@feng2023; @silver2017].
note: Supports PRM as prefix value. Beam and tree search and AlphaZero shape are not in this quote.
